comparison: Major disagreement on interpretation. OpenEval finds the synapse specificity mechanism well-supported (C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C37, C63, C64), while peer reviewers challenge this interpretation as not directly addressed by the data. Reviewers accept the muscle differentiation program but request substantial revision to focus on muscle arm formation rather than synapse specificity claims.

Both address lin-12(wy750) characterization (C15, C16, C17, C24, C25, C26, C27). OpenEval finds the dosage hypothesis well-supported though alternative explanations not fully excluded. Peer reviewers are uncertain whether the phenotype represents partial fate switch or selective disruption of muscle arm growth, requesting additional fate markers and morphological analysis.

Both address developmental timing aspects (C28, C29, C68, C69). OpenEval finds temperature-shift experiments demonstrate late L4 requirement. Peer reviewers accept the timing data as part of the muscle differentiation program but want clearer discussion of whether this represents fate specification or selective disruption.

Strong agreement on functional importance of muscle arms. Both accept behavioral assays, calcium imaging (C18, C19, C20, C21, C22, C23), and postsynaptic marker enrichment (C65, C66) as documenting physiological relevance. Peer reviewers acknowledge this documents muscle cell participation in synapse development through muscle arm formation.

Strong agreement on molecular pathway. Both accept expression analysis (C43, C45, C47), down-regulation in mutants (C44, C46, C48), LAG-1 binding sites (C50, C51), and functional rescue (C52). OpenEval notes direct binding not demonstrated for C49. Peer reviewers accept this as part of muscle differentiation program without specific concerns.

Disagreement on interpretation of downstream effectors. OpenEval finds UNC-40/MADD-2 pathway well-supported (C42-C52, C72). Peer reviewers accept the molecular pathway data but challenge the 'postsynaptic target selection' interpretation (C64, C72) as not directly addressed, consistent with their broader concern about synapse specificity claims.

Agreement on ectopic expression experiments. Both accept that UNC-40 can induce muscle arms in vm1 (C53, C54, C55, C56). OpenEval finds this demonstrates sufficiency and suggests guidance mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting UNC-40's role in muscle arm formation program.

Agreement on genetic interactions. Both accept double mutant analysis (C57), cross-rescue experiments (C58, C59), and expression independence (C61). OpenEval notes some ambiguity in the 'synergistic but parallel' model (C60, C62). Peer reviewers accept the genetic interaction data documenting cooperation in muscle arm formation.

Strong agreement on independence of pre- and postsynaptic development. Both accept cell ablation experiments (C12, C13) and developmental timing observations (C73, C74). OpenEval notes this challenges traditional bidirectional signaling models. Peer reviewers accept this as documenting muscle differentiation preceding postsynaptic differentiation.

Agreement on cell-autonomous requirements and pathway logic. Both accept cell-specific rescue (C33, C34), dominant-negative LAG-1 (C35), and expression analysis (C32, C36). OpenEval finds cellular logic clearly established. Peer reviewers accept this documents the pathway but want interpretation focused on muscle differentiation rather than synapse specificity.

Agreement on feedback regulation mechanism. Both accept expression analysis in mutant backgrounds (C36, C38), LAG-1 binding sites in lin-12 promoter (C39), and lin-12(e2621) analysis (C40, C41, C70). OpenEval finds positive feedback model well-supported. Peer reviewers accept this as part of molecular pathway controlling muscle differentiation.

Agreement on differential guidance by epithelial cells. Both accept APX-1 expression patterns (C32 referenced in OpenEval R7), anatomical observations (C75, C76, C77, C78, C79), and organizational role of epithelial cells. OpenEval notes some speculation about specific mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept this integrative model as reasonable interpretation.

Strong agreement on anatomical foundations. Both accept established anatomical knowledge (C7, C8, C9), EM reconstruction confirmation (C10), and fluorescence imaging (C11). OpenEval views this as essential context. Peer reviewers accept this as establishing the system for studying muscle arm development and postsynaptic differentiation.

Agreement with shared uncertainty. OpenEval finds lin-3 mutant data (C14) limited by pleiotropy and guidance cue identity (C71) speculative, requiring further investigation. Peer reviewers did not raise specific concerns, accepting these observations as consistent with epithelial cell involvement, though OpenEval's uncertainty is more explicit.

Disagreement on overall interpretation. OpenEval R1 encompasses broad mechanism including muscle arm generation and target selection (C64 among others). Peer R14 specifically challenges the 'postsynaptic target selection' interpretation while accepting muscle arm generation, reflecting the fundamental interpretive disagreement about synapse specificity claims.
